title: Start small
claim: Begin with a manageable amount of strength work and add work gradually as you learn how you recover.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Choose a repeatable schedule
claim: Choose training days you can repeat consistently within your other commitments.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Allow recovery time
claim: Leave time between demanding sessions for the same muscles and adjust if soreness or fatigue persists.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Practice movement
claim: Use a controllable load while learning a movement and prioritize consistent technique.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Select a squat pattern
claim: A squat pattern can train the legs; choose a version that fits available equipment and comfortable range.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Select a hinge pattern
claim: A hip hinge is one option for training the posterior chain; choose a variation you can control.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Select a horizontal push
claim: A push-up or press can provide a horizontal pushing pattern when appropriate for the person and equipment.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Select a horizontal pull
claim: A row can provide a horizontal pulling pattern; select a variation that fits the available equipment.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Select a vertical push
claim: An overhead press is one option for a vertical push if the movement is comfortable.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Select a vertical pull
claim: A pull-up or pulldown can provide a vertical pulling pattern if suitable equipment is available.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Use single-leg work
claim: A split squat or step-up can add single-leg work when it fits balance and available support.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Consider a trunk exercise
claim: A plank is one option for practicing trunk stability; choose a duration that preserves control.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Match exercise to equipment
claim: Check every required item, including benches, racks and bars, before selecting an exercise.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Choose a substitute by pattern
claim: When replacing an exercise, compare movement, equipment and comfort rather than relying on the name alone.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Adapt to range of motion
claim: Use a range you can control and adjust the exercise if the available range is uncomfortable.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Set an initial load
claim: Choose an initial load you can lift with consistent form while leaving some repetitions in reserve.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Keep load unspecified
claim: When ability or equipment is unknown, leave the load for the person to choose rather than inventing a weight.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Progress repetitions first
claim: One progression option is to add repetitions within a chosen range before increasing load.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Progress load gradually
claim: After completing the planned repetitions with good control, consider a small load increase next time.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Repeat a load
claim: If a new load makes technique inconsistent, repeat or reduce it while practicing the movement.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Change one variable
claim: When adjusting training, consider changing one of load, repetitions or sets at a time so the response is easier to interpret.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Use a repetition range
claim: A repetition range allows a person to progress within the same load before adjusting it.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Rest between sets
claim: Rest long enough to perform the next set with the intended technique and effort.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Use effort as a guide
claim: Repetitions in reserve describe how many additional repetitions a person estimates they could perform with good form.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Avoid forced maximums
claim: A useful training session does not require testing a maximal lift; select loads suited to the session.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Track working sets
claim: Record sets and repetitions consistently so future changes can be compared with the original plan.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Adjust total work
claim: If a workload is hard to recover from, consider reducing sets or spacing the work across sessions.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Build volume gradually
claim: When adding sets, make small changes and observe how performance and recovery respond.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Distribute work
claim: Spreading planned work across available days is one way to manage session length.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Set a time limit
claim: For a short session, prioritize a few relevant movements and leave sufficient time for warm-up and rest.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Warm up specifically
claim: Before harder sets, practice the movement with lighter effort appropriate to the exercise.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Plan around sleep
claim: Consider sleep and other stressors when deciding whether to maintain or reduce a demanding session.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Respond to persistent fatigue
claim: If fatigue persists, consider reducing training demands and seek qualified advice when needed.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Take symptoms seriously
claim: Stop an exercise that causes concerning pain and seek an appropriate qualified professional for assessment.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Interpret a missed session
claim: A missed session alone does not establish a trend; resume with a practical schedule rather than compensating automatically.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Interpret a short history
claim: A few recorded workouts may be too little evidence to identify a reliable performance trend.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Separate plan and completion
claim: A planned set is not evidence that the set was completed; use completed records for history claims.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Treat missing load as unknown
claim: A missing recorded weight is unknown and should not be assumed to be zero.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Compare like with like
claim: Compare similar exercises, units and repetition targets before drawing conclusions from recorded sets.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Account for individual context
claim: Adjust exercise choices to the person’s goals, experience, equipment and response rather than using a universal plan.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Strength emphasis
claim: For a strength-oriented goal, practice the selected lifts regularly with loads and repetition targets the person can manage.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Muscle-building emphasis
claim: For a muscle-building goal, choose exercises that can be performed consistently and progressed over time.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Plan easier sessions
claim: If a session must be easier, reducing load or sets is an option while keeping movements familiar.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.

title: Review after changes
claim: After changing a plan, compare recorded performance and recovery over several sessions before making another large change.
applicability: General adult strength training; adapt to individual circumstances. Not diagnosis or rehabilitation.
